results.title: Exhibition: Taixu in Singapore: A 100-Year Commemoration
results.description:
Taixu (1890–1947) was one of the most influential Chinese Buddhist monks of the 20th century, best known for his efforts to modernise Buddhism and make it relevant to a rapidly changing world.

Commemorating the centenary of Taixu’s first visit to Singapore in 1926, the exhibition Taixu in Singapore: A 100-Year Commemoration brings renewed attention to his enduring influence on the development of Buddhism in Singapore and the wider region.

results.title: Researcher Unbound Symposium 2026
results.description:
AI & Open Science: Navigating the Future of Research

Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming the research landscape. From accelerating discovery and scholarly communication to redefining the way research is conducted, AI presents unprecedented opportunities along with challenges on research integrity, transparency, and trust. At the same time, open science has never been more important. As research becomes increasingly collaborative and data-driven, open science principles are essential to ensuring that knowledge remains credible, reusable, and impactful.

 

Join us at Researcher Unbound Symposium 2026, where leading researchers, practitioners, and thought leaders across industries converge in a one-day exploration of how AI and open science are reshaping the future of research.

results.title: RUS2026 Taster Workshop 1: Use of AI in Systematic Review Searching
results.description:
Generative AI is rapidly changing how systematic reviews are conducted. From literature searching, search results screening, data extraction, quality assessment, to manuscript writing, AI can support each stage of the systematic review process. In this practical session, explore the use of chatbots to deepen your understanding of systematic search strategies, discover tools that can help you be more efficient and more!


Learn:

  • To leverage AI in developing and executing search strategies
  • To evaluate AI-generated search strategies for completeness, accuracy, and relevance
  • AI tools available to empower your systematic review workflow
results.more_info:
About the Speakers:

Wong Suei Nee |  Senior Librarian, NUS Libraries

Suei Nee has more than 10 years of experience working as a Librarian. Her work interests include Systematic Review searching and teaching users how to search for full-text articles. She has worked in both the Central Library and Medical Library, and relishes the different learning experiences both libraries offer. She is also part of the Scholarly Communications and Systematic Review Team.

 

Annelisa Chin |  Senior Librarian, NUS Libraries

Annelissa enjoys working with students and researchers through systematic review consultations and workshops, where she shares the methodology and best practices for systematic literature search.

results.title: RUS2026 Taster Workshop 2: Peer Benchmarking Like a Pro Using SciVal
results.description:
Looking to demonstrate your research impact? Curious how your research ranks in the global research landscape? Or evaluating research strengths across researchers? In this hands-on taster workshop, you’ll learn how to use SciVal to generate research metrics and benchmark research performance. Whether you're an individual researcher or supporting research strategy, you'll leave with practical skills to make the most of SciVal.

Learn:

  • To identify appropriate research impact metrics such as H-index, FWCI or publications in top journal percentiles
  • Effective search strategies to identify researchers and analyse their research impact
  • To compile a benchmarking table to compare researchers across a range of research metrics
results.more_info:
About the Speaker:

Richard Ho |  Principal Librarian (Scholarly Communications), NUS Libraries

Richard leads the Scholarly Communications Team at NUS Libraries, working closely with the NUS community to support and advance initiatives in academic publishing, open access, research impact, research data management, and NUS' institutional repository, ScholarBank@NUS.
